key_insight: Quantization errors in recurrent states are not equally harmful: their impact depends on when they occur and where in the state they land. STEPQuant shows that preserving the most error-sensitive parts of long-lived memory can avoid major accuracy loss while still reducing memory use.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the memory bottleneck of linear-attention models with recurrent states during concurrent serving. Naively quantizing these persistent states to low precision often causes large accuracy degradation because errors accumulate across repeated state updates.
method: Analyzes quantization error through two lenses: temporal persistence and spatial sensitivity within the recurrent state.
Identifies which state components and decoding steps are most vulnerable to error propagation.
Applies selective, error-aware state quantization to reduce memory usage while minimizing accuracy loss.
impact: This makes low-precision recurrent-state serving more practical for real-world deployment, especially under high concurrency. Practitioners can lower memory cost without blindly sacrificing model quality.

paper_title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
paper_authors: Bingchen Yao, Haobo Xu, Haokun Lin, Yichen Wu, Ziyu Guo
